answer: Because the basalt ordering is published with the voyage batch, the wander audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early as a result gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 38% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Honest users pay that once, farms 21 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
